title: Reviews and Enhancements to Sports Excellence Awards to Support Elite Athletes' Training, Welfare and Long-term Development
what_it_is: Reviews and Enhancements to Sports Excellence Awards to Support Elite Athletes' Training, Welfare and Long-term Development

sections.label: spex athlete support growth
sections.summary: Singapore now supports over 1,500 carded athletes across 55 sports, up from 272 athletes and 14 sports in 1993, with spexPotential added in 2024.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
sentences.text: Today, we support more than 1,500 carded athletes across 55 sports, compared to 272 athletes across 14 sports when we first started spex in 1993.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
sentences.text: This is a 450% increase in the number of athletes supported and 350% increase in the number of sports supported.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
sentences.text: For example, in recent years, we introduced the spexPotential programme in 2024 to enhance support for younger athletes making the transition to higher levels of sporting success.

sections.label: Games frequency and review
sections.summary: The Olympic, Commonwealth and Asian Games are held every four years and the SEA Games every two, and Mr Yam's suggestion will be considered in the review.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
sentences.text: The Olympic, Commonwealth and Asian Games, for example, they have more competitive fields, take place every four years, while SEA Games takes place every two.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
sentences.text: We will take to heart Mr Yam's suggestion, and request for it to be considered in their review.

sections.label: SEA Games cash incentive review
sections.summary: A Member asks the Minister for a timeline for SportSG and SNOC's review of cash incentives for SEA Games silver and bronze medalists.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Could the Minister share with us what is a possible timeline by which SportSG will be working with SNOC on the review of cash incentives and recognition for our SEA Games medalists, especially those who are in silver and bronze categories?

sentences.speaker: Mr David Neo
sentences.text: It is my understanding that SNOC has recently concluded the review.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Neo
sentences.text: And I believe they should be ready to announce the updated Awards in due course.

sections.label: spex and SSP medal shares
sections.summary: At the last SEA Games, spex Scholars and spexPotential recipients won half the medals and almost nine in 10 golds, while SSP students and alumni took about a third of medals and almost half the golds.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Neo
sentences.text: Going by the last SEA Games, what we have observed is that our spex Scholars as well as our spex Potential recipients won half of our medals and almost nine out of 10 of every gold medal that was won, In the same way, our SSP students and alumni also accounted for about a third of our medals and almost half of our gold medals.

sections.label: School Sports Fiesta access
sections.summary: Last year the School Sports Fiesta was announced as a way to broaden sport access for young children from all backgrounds, including lower-income families.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Neo
sentences.text: On her second question about improving sport access, especially for children from lower-income families, last year we announced the School Sports Fiesta, which is one of those ways in which to broaden sport access to young children from all backgrounds.
